steps.title: Import Redux Toolkit and Vuex
steps.instruction: Import createSlice and createAsyncThunk from '@reduxjs/toolkit' and createStore from 'vuex'.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in the necessary functions from their respective packages.

successCriteria: createSlice, createAsyncThunk, and createStore are imported from their respective packages.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported the required Redux Toolkit and Vuex functions.

steps.title: Create initial state object
steps.instruction: Define an initial state object with properties for data (an empty array), loading (a boolean set to false), and error (a string set to null).
steps.hint: Create a plain JavaScript object with the required properties and their initial values.

steps.expectedOutcome: An initial state object is defined with the correct structure and default values.
successCriteria: The initial state object has properties: data (empty array), loading (false), and error (null).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've correctly defined the initial state structure with all required properties and their default values.

steps.title: Create async thunk for API simulation
steps.instruction: Using the imported createAsyncThunk, create an async thunk named 'fetchData' that simulates fetching data with a 1-second delay and returns a mock data object.
steps.hint: createAsyncThunk takes a type string and an async payload creator function. Use setTimeout to simulate a delay.
steps.expectedOutcome: An async thunk named 'fetchData' is created that simulates an API call with delay.
successCriteria: The fetchData async thunk is defined using createAsyncThunk, includes a 1-second delay simulation, and returns mock data.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created an async thunk that simulates API data fetching with a delay.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your async thunk includes the delay simulation and returns mock data.
steps.feedbackWrong: The async thunk isn't quite right. Check that you're using createAsyncThunk correctly and simulating a delay.

steps.title: Create slice with reducers
steps.instruction: Create a slice using createSlice with the name 'dataSlice', the initialState object, and an empty reducers object.
steps.hint: Call createSlice with an object containing name, initialState, and reducers properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: A dataSlice constant is created using createSlice with the required properties.
successCriteria: The slice is created with name 'dataSlice', uses the initialState object, and includes an empty reducers object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the slice with the required structure.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using createSlice with name 'dataSlice', the initialState, and an empty reducers object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The slice wasn't created correctly. Check that you're using createSlice with the required properties.

steps.title: Create Vuex store with the slice
steps.instruction: Create a Vuex store using createStore and register the slice reducer you created earlier. The store should be exported as a default export.
steps.hint: Use createStore from vuex and pass an object with a modules property containing your slice reducer.
steps.expectedOutcome: A Vuex store is created and exported, with your Redux Toolkit slice reducer registered as a module.
successCriteria: createStore is called with an object containing modules
The slice reducer is registered in the modules object
The store is exported as default
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a Vuex store and integrated your Redux Toolkit slice reducer as a module.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using createStore from vuex and properly registering your slice reducer in the modules object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Vuex store wasn't created correctly. Remember to use createStore from vuex and pass an object with a modules property containing your slice reducer.

steps.title: Create Vue component structure
steps.instruction: Create a Vue component named 'DataDisplay' with a template section containing a basic div wrapper and a heading that says 'Data Display Component'.
steps.hint: Define a Vue component with a template that includes a div element and an h2 heading inside it.
steps.expectedOutcome: A Vue component named 'DataDisplay' is created with a template containing a div wrapper and an h2 heading.
successCriteria: The component is named 'DataDisplay' and has a template with a div element containing an h2 heading with the text 'Data Display Component'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the Vue component structure with the required template elements.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a component, but it's missing either the correct name, the div wrapper, or the h2 heading with the specified text.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component structure doesn't match the requirements. Make sure to create a Vue component named 'DataDisplay' with a template containing a div and an h2 heading.

steps.title: Add computed properties for state access
steps.instruction: Inside your Vue component, add a computed property that returns the data value from the Vuex store state.
steps.hint: Use the computed function from Vue to create a property that accesses store.state.data.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a computed property that maps to the data value from the store state.
successCriteria: A computed property named 'data' is defined in the component that returns this.$store.state.data
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a computed property to access the store data.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your computed property correctly returns this.$store.state.data.
steps.feedbackWrong: The computed property is missing or doesn't correctly access the store data. Try using computed: { data() { return this.$store.state.data; } }

steps.title: Add methods to dispatch actions
steps.instruction: In your Vue component, add a method named 'fetchData' that dispatches the async thunk using 'this.$store.dispatch'.
steps.hint: Create a methods object in your component with a fetchData method that calls this.$store.dispatch with the async thunk action.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a method that can dispatch the async thunk to fetch data.
successCriteria: A 'fetchData' method is added to the component's methods object that dispatches the async thunk using this.$store.dispatch.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a method to dispatch the async thunk action.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added a 'fetchData' method that calls this.$store.dispatch with the async thunk.
steps.feedbackWrong: The method isn't quite right. Check that you've added a 'fetchData' method to the methods object that dispatches the async thunk.

steps.title: Add UI elements to display state
steps.instruction: In your component's template, add a <div> element that conditionally displays the fetched data, loading status, and error messages based on the current state.
steps.hint: Use Vue's template syntax with v-if or v-show directives to show different UI elements depending on the computed properties for data, loading, and error.
steps.analogousExample: // Example: conditional display in Vue template
steps.expectedOutcome: The component template now includes conditional rendering logic to display the current state values (data, loading, error) appropriately.
successCriteria: Template contains a <div> with conditional rendering that displays loading status, error messages, and fetched data based on the computed properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added UI elements that conditionally display the state values. This completes the state display functionality.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some UI elements, but make sure you have conditional rendering for all three state properties: loading, error, and data.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template doesn't yet properly display the state values. Review how to use conditional rendering in Vue templates with v-if/v-else.

steps.title: Add buttons and wire click handlers
steps.instruction: Add two buttons inside your Vue component's template: one labeled 'Fetch Data' that calls the method to dispatch the async thunk, and another labeled 'Reset' that calls the method to dispatch the reset action.
steps.hint: Use the @click directive to bind each button to its corresponding method. Place the buttons inside the template section of your component.
steps.analogousExample: // Adding buttons with click handlers in Vue
steps.expectedOutcome: Two buttons appear in the UI: 'Fetch Data' and 'Reset'. Clicking 'Fetch Data' triggers the async thunk to simulate fetching data, and clicking 'Reset' dispatches the reset action to clear the state.
successCriteria: The component template contains two <button> elements with @click directives bound to the fetchData and resetData methods, and the buttons are labeled 'Fetch Data' and 'Reset'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the buttons and wired them to the correct action dispatchers. The UI now has controls to fetch and reset data.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some buttons, but make sure both buttons are present with correct labels and @click bindings to the appropriate methods.
steps.feedbackWrong: The buttons are missing or not correctly wired. Ensure you add two <button> elements with @click="fetchData" and @click="resetData" inside the template.
